Definition: from G1 (as negative particle); and G1160; costless, i.e. gratuitous:--without expense.
BiblicalUsage: Without expense, free of charge — adapanos appears once, in Paul's boast: he preached the gospel "without charge," refusing payment "that I abuse not my power in the gospel." He had the right to be paid; he gave the right up, so no one could say he sold the message.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for 'without charge' is a small thing, and Paul's boast is the sermon — he would rather work with his own hands than let the gospel look bought.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
